# Kin-ming Liu

Affiliations:

_South China Morning Post_

Links:

[My First Trip](http://www.chinafile.com/reporting-opinion/my-first-trip)

Kin-ming Liu, a Hong Kong-based journalist, is a ChinaFile Fellow at the Asia Society's Center on U.S.-China Relations and edits ChinaFile's [My First Trip section](http://www.chinafile.com/reporting-opinion/my-first-trip) . Liu is currently deputy chief editor of Multi-Media Content at SCMPChinese.com, a forthcoming Chinese-language website of the _South China Morning Post ( [SCMP](http://www.scmp.com/) )_ . Prior to his arrival at the _SCMP_ , Liu spent 5 years at the _Hong Kong Economic Journal_ , where he played a number of different roles. He was also a blogger at _PostGlobal_ , a global debate blog on international affairs and foreign policy run in partnership by _The Washington Post_ and _Newsweek_ .

Previously, Liu was a columnist based in Washington, D.C. He wrote for _The New York Sun_ , _The Hong Kong Standard_ , and other publications.

...

In 1998 he was the winner of a Hong Kong Human Rights Press Award for English-language commentary.

Liu is the editor of a collection of pieces from the _Hong Kong Economic Journal_ 's “ [My First Trip to China](http://www.hkej.com/template/features/html/first_trip/index.jsp) ” series was published by Muse in 2012.

_Last Updated: April 3, 2014_

London-based Luxury Journalist

Ming Liu is a luxury journalist who contributes regularly to the New York Times, Financial Times and CNN. Her work has also appeared in The Economist’s 1843 and other publications, covering topics from watches and jewellery to Chinese art, travel and haute cuisine. She graduated from Wellesley College and, after earning a master’s in creative writing at the University of Manchester, she published her first novel, Our Man in China, about American-born Chinese trying to make in the Middle Kingdom.
